subject: maths
title: Adding: putting groups together
intro: Adding means putting things together to find how many there are altogether. If you have some toys and a friend gives you more, adding tells you how many you have now. This gentle lesson shows adding with pictures first, then the quick way to count on.

sections.heading: Adding is putting together
body: When we **add**, we join two groups and count them all. The plus sign **+** means 'and', and the equals sign **=** means 'is the same as'. So **3 + 2** means 'three things and two more things', and it equals **5**.
Look at the picture: three dots and two more dots make five dots when we count them all together.

sections.heading: Counting on
body: You don't always have to count every dot from the start. A quicker way is to **count on**: start at the bigger number and count up by the smaller one. For **4 + 3**, start at 4 and count on three more — 5, 6, 7. The answer is 7.
Counting on your fingers is a great way to do this. Hold up the first number, then count on the second number one finger at a time.

steps: Where you stop is the answer.

sections.heading: A helpful trick: order doesn't matter
body: Here is something nice about adding: you can add in **any order** and get the same answer. **2 + 5** is the same as **5 + 2** — both make 7. So you can always start with the bigger number to make counting on easier.
This means if you know 3 + 4 = 7, you also already know 4 + 3 = 7. Learning one fact gives you two.

practice.explain: The plus sign + means add — put the groups together and count them all.
Three and two more makes five: 3 + 2 = 5.

practice.q: To add 5 + 2 by counting on, where do you start?
practice.explain: Start at the bigger number (5) and count on the smaller one: 6, 7. So 5 + 2 = 7.
Order doesn't matter in adding, so 3 + 6 is also 9.
Four and four more makes eight: 4 + 4 = 8.

summary: Adding means putting groups together and counting them all; + means 'and', = means 'is the same as'.
You can 'count on' from the bigger number instead of counting everything from the start.
Order doesn't matter: 2 + 5 is the same as 5 + 2.
